investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-19T08:59–09:07Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path exists, so pods remain Unschedulable for ~143–146 seconds before the eval timeout fires and zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is collected.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node can accept a new remote-agent pod. Because the pod never schedules, the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent called with machineType "remote") never reaches the point where it can write vmIdPresent or remoteState evidence, causing a total contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent workloads or leaked/zombie VMs are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy. If those 2 nodes were also at capacity for other reasons (e.g., node pressure, DaemonSet overhead), the effective schedulable pool is zero. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval runs: all three sibling checks ran sequentially and each encountered the same exhaustion, suggesting the capacity shortage persisted for at least ~7 minutes (08:59–09:07Z). This could indicate a steady-state capacity deficit rather than a transient spike.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — leaked or non-terminated remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is responsible for teardown; if a prior run's cleanup failed, VM slots may remain occupied. No direct evidence of cleanup failure is present in the packet.

investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. This prevented the remote agent pod from starting, which in turn prevented the eval runner from obtaining an orgId, agentId, readyState, or state — the four fields required by the remote-agent-state expected-output contract. investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Swarm Nodes Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every agent pod submitted by the eval runner was stuck unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No pod ever started, so no runtime response was produced and all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints, leaving only 2 schedulable nodes, both of which report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm". Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window remained Unschedulable for ~143–146 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence payload and a contract violation across all three remote-agents checks. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
